name: Algebraic pc-Minor Dictionary
statement: For an isometrically embedded family $X\subseteq Q_E$, its complementary-literal ideal $J_X=(\prod_{e\in E}v_{e,1-x_e}:x\in X)$ has linear quotients exactly when $X$ is dismantlable ample. If a pc-minor $K=\pi_D(X_f)$ conditions coordinates $F$ to a realized word $f$ and contracts disjoint coordinates $D$, then $J_K=\phi_{f,D}(J_X)$, where the conditioned matching literals map to zero, their opposites to one, and both literals of every contracted color to one. Consequently, $X$ is pc-minimal outside dismantlable ampleness exactly when $J_X$ lacks linear quotients but every proper specialization of this form has them.
proof: The monomial-colon formula identifies variable-generated colons with the condition that every earlier concept has a previously inserted cube neighbor of the new concept in their Boolean interval. Induction on Hamming distance makes this equivalent to every prefix being isometric, hence to a reversed corner peeling. Under the displayed specialization, a generator from the wrong conditioned side vanishes, a generator from the retained side loses all conditioned and contracted factors, and its remaining product is exactly the generator of the projected concept; repetitions do not change the ideal. The normal form of a pc-minor as conditioning followed by contractions gives the minimal-obstruction clause.
